doc.ownership: Every emitted Flycast config line, native action name, and SDL scancode lives in this declaration. The emitter only validates the rows against emulator.json, steam_input.json, and steamdeck.skm before rendering them.
doc.gameplay: The generated keyboard mapping is action-only. Flycast's upstream SDL GameController mapping remains responsible for Dreamcast gameplay, analog triggers, Start, D-pad, and rumble.
doc.hotkeys: Flycast version-4 combo rows use simultaneous SDL scancodes (sequential=0): Left Ctrl is 224; A/S/J/K/X are 4/22/13/14/27. They invoke Flycast's native load/save/slot/screenshot actions (core/input/mapping.cpp:50-72). Its own menu (btn_menu) and exit (btn_escape) are not bound: ui.menu and app.quit are Semu's, or Ctrl+M would open Flycast's settings over Semu's menu.
doc.state: No external save path is configured. Flycast therefore stores per-game VMUs and save states in the isolated XDG_DATA_HOME/flycast tree declared by emulator.json.
doc.disc_picker: emu.cfg [config] BoxartDisplayMode = no and FetchBoxart = no: in box-art mode the Insert Disk picker shows every disc of a game as the same cover and title, so the discs of a playlist could not be told apart. List mode shows the (Disc N).chd file names, and nothing is fetched from TheGamesDB.
doc.save_states: Flycast cycles ten slots and wraps (cycleSaveStateSlot, core/ui/gui.cpp:518-522), shows slot + 1 (gui.cpp:1620-1624) and saves the choice to emu.cfg [config] Dreamcast.SavestateSlot; Semu pins it to 0 each launch, where its own counter starts.
doc.keys: Flycast 2.7 reads its options as dotted keys in [config] (upstream_keys). Until the M16 review Semu wrote [rend] and [Dreamcast] blocks Flycast never read, so OpenGL was only its default, and rend.WidescreenGameHacks = yes never applied; it is now written as no, the picture the owner has played (the widescreen cheats would draw an anamorphic 16:9 picture inside the 4:3 TV). The dead [input] enable_x11_keyboard line (only Flycast's man page names it) is gone.
doc.osd: config/emulators/flycast/semu-no-osd.patch: Flycast draws its loading screen and its toasts with ImGui into the frames it swaps, so Semu's swap hook composed them as game: the Deck's boot film (2026-10-06) showed the Starting... box inside the TV for about 0.8 s before the BIOS. Flycast 2.7 has no option for either. The patch keeps the loader's state changes (gui.cpp gui_display_loadscreen) and draws neither the box (Loading..., Starting..., the progress bar) nor the box art behind it, so the TV stays black until the game draws; and the in-game toasts os_notify shows (State saved, Save state slot N, Screenshot saved; gui.cpp:773-784, nullDC.cpp:250, gui.cpp:1623 and 1697) go to Flycast's log instead, since Semu toasts the actions it sends. Semu's build is only ever launched with a game.
doc.pacing: rend.vsync = yes with config/emulators/flycast/semu-swap-interval.patch (M16 item 8, "super laggy at like 23fps on sonic adventure"). Flycast 5aa091fd paces the emulation by its audio (every push waits for room: config::LimitFPS is constexpr true, option.h:375, audiostream.cpp:59, audiobackend_sdl2.cpp:126-139) and, with vsync, by its swap: the emulator thread waits for the render thread (Renderer_if.cpp:59-109, 592-593), which presents only the frames the game draws (rend.DelayFrameSwapping, Renderer_if.cpp:243) and swaps every refresh / 60 times the game's own interval, truncated (wsi/sdl.cpp:86-96 and 137-153; the game's interval from SwapIntervalDetector, Renderer_if.cpp:297-365). Game Mode runs the Deck OLED's screen at 90 Hz (89.89 by xrandr on its display): a scene the game draws at 30 frames a second (Sonic Adventure's movies, story scenes and Speed Highway's demo) asked for 3 refreshes and took 4 under gamescope, 22.5 frames per second, and the game ran at 75% (off-screen at 90 Hz, the HUD clock gained 1.87 s in 2.5 s). The patch swaps at the next refresh wherever the refresh is not a whole multiple of 60 Hz, so the audio paces the game there; 60 and 120 Hz keep Flycast's own interval, whose frames come evenly (17 ms apart at 60 Hz, 34 ms for a 30-frame scene; with vsync off they bunched to the audio callbacks, 22 and 44 ms). rend.ThreadedRendering and rend.DelayFrameSwapping are Flycast's defaults, pinned because the measurement holds for them.

native_shortcuts.why: GamepadDevice::find_mapping uses mappings/SDL_Keyboard.cfg whenever it exists; KeyboardInputMapping's defaults (bare X, C, S, D as Dreamcast buttons, Tab for the menu, Space for fast forward) apply only without the file. Semu writes the whole file with empty [digital] and [analog] sections, so a chord like Ctrl+S presses no Dreamcast button. A per-game SDL_Keyboard_<id>.cfg the owner makes would still win.

upstream_keys.source: flycast v2.7 (5aa091fde632fb332c8d8c34e280d62dc951954c): core/cfg/option.cpp:28-252 (every Option, its section config unless named; option.h:107 defaults it) with option.h:409-434 (RendererOption, pvr.rend); core/sdl/sdl.cpp:789-794 ([window] left, top, width, height, fullscreen, maximized). Flycast reads no [rend] or [Dreamcast] section: those options are dotted keys in [config]. Every key Semu writes to emu.cfg must be one of these (a contract checks it), so a pin that Flycast ignores cannot pass for a setting.
